Hi everyone,

I am using R for the first time for my dissertation and have a pretty big model to test. I have already parceled the data due to a smaller sample size. When I try to run the SEM model, basically nothing happens. It looks like it is continually running something (I ran it for over 30 minutes today). Then, when I press stop, I sometimes get a message about indicators being negative, but sometimes I do not.

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Getting a model to run with parcels & a lot of mediators
parts:
Alex,
I do not have a solution, only a strategy.  Here is what I would do in our situation:

1. Remove the bootstrapping.  Get the model to run first, then rerun it with bootstrapping.
2. Check to make sure that the parameters related to the single-indicator factor are estimable.  Try fixing the unique variance to see if that makes the difference.
3. If you cannot get the model to run, try fitting just a CFA model first.  Then add the structural model once you work out the bugs in the CFA.
4. If you cannot get the full CFA to run, try running subsets of factors before fitting the full model.
5. If possible, construct 4 parcels for each factor.  If not possible, construct at least 3.

Keith

On 02/13/2017 02:08 AM, Alex wrote:
> Hi everyone,
>

> big model to test. I have already parceled the data due to a smaller
> sample size. When I try to run the SEM model, basically nothing happens.
> It looks like it is continually running something (I ran it for over 30
> minutes today).
You are requesting a bootstrap-based test statistic:

This may take a long time indeed. To see what happens, add the verbose =
TRUE argument. Just let it run for a night.

You may also consider using estimator = "MLR" instead (and remove the
test= "boot" argument).

Yves.
